description: Add a compact always-visible expedition depth milestone readout that shows the next ore band or Motherlode target and the remaining meters, so miners can judge progress without opening Info / Cargo or mentally subtracting approximate depths.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh before development, preserve the React-before-runtime startup order, and retain existing DOM IDs/classes consumed by src/dom.ts and src/game.ts.

Inspect src/constants.ts ORES/WORLD_H/START_Y, src/prospecting.ts depth helpers, src/objective.ts milestone logic, src/game.ts HUD lifecycle, src/ui.tsx hooks, src/dom.ts, src/styles.css, and current Vitest coverage. Extract a small DOM-free formatter/classifier that derives the next meaningful depth landmark and non-negative remaining meters from shared world/ore data without duplicating depth literals.

Add one stable compact HUD hook near the objective/scanner/fuel guidance that distinguishes the starter seam, next locked ore band, and Motherlode approach with actionable copy such as the target name and meters deeper; keep it synchronized after movement, drilling, load, reset, game-over, and return-to-surface paths.

Make the readout readable on desktop and a 390×844 phone viewport without crowding existing objective, terrain scanner, fuel reserve, cargo value, or service guidance, and ensure Info / Cargo still visually covers the underlying HUD and keyboard/touch input remains unchanged.

Add DOM-free unit tests for starter/ore-band/Motherlode target selection and remaining-distance formatting plus React/runtime hook coverage. Run ./init.sh and live desktop and 390×844 CDP smokes that start the game, descend through the starter seam toward a later ore milestone, observe the readout update, open/close Info / Cargo, resume movement, and collect runtime exceptions.
acceptance: Players can always see the next meaningful depth target and how many meters remain, with a clear transition from the starter seam through locked ore bands to the Motherlode approach; values are derived from live depth and shared game data rather than hard-coded UI numbers.

The milestone readout stays accurate after movement, drilling, load, reset, game-over, and surface-return paths and does not regress existing HUD guidance, modal layering, desktop/phone layout, or keyboard/touch controls.
DOM-free milestone logic and React/runtime hook coverage pass, and live desktop/phone browser smokes confirm the readout reacts during gameplay with no runtime exceptions.
Before marking complete, follow miner-daily-task-runner and run ./init.sh, ./test.sh, npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build as fresh final verification.
